subject: general
question: Where in the body is villi found?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Small intestine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **villi **of the **small intestine project **into the **intestinal cavity**.
 
• It **greatly increases **the **surface area **for **food absorption **and **adds digestive secretions**.
 
• The **villi number **about **10 to 40 per square millimeter **(**6,000 to 25,000 per square inch**) **of tissue**.
 
• **Small Intestine**:
 
 
• The **small intestine **has **three parts**:
 
 
• the duodenum,jejunum, and ileum.
 
 
 
• It **helps **to **further digest food coming **from the **stomach**.
 
• It **absorbs nutrients **(vitamins, minerals, carbohydrates, fats, proteins) and water from food so they can be used by the body.
 
• The **small intestine **is **part of the digestive system**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The long**, **tube-like organ **is **connected to the small intestine **at **one end **and the **anus at the other**. The **large intestine **has **four parts**: the **cecum**, **colon**, **rectum**, and **anal canal**. **Partly digested food moves through **the **cecum into the colon**, where **water **and **some nutrients, and electrolytes are removed**.
 
• The **liver **is **your largest internal organ**. About the **size of a football**, it's **located mainly **in the **upper right portion **of your **abdomen **— **beneath **the **diaphragm **and **above your stomach**. A **small portion extends **into the **upper left quadrant**. The **liver **is an **organ **about the **size of a football**.
 
• The **stomach **is **a J-shaped organ **that **digests food**. It **produces enzymes **(substances that create chemical reactions) and acids (digestive juices). **This mix of enzymes **and **digestive juices breaks down **food so it **can pass to your small intestine**.
